messages:
vikram: quick bench comparing prefetch 'peek' heuristic vs 'evict-first' across A100/H100 in us-east and eu-west. TL;DR: peek reduces p50/p95 for mixed seqlen distro, evict-first edges out on tokens/s at very high concurrency. logs below.

vikram: ```
# GPU,region,heuristic,concurrency,seqlen_mix,hit_rate,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,tokens_s
A100,us-east,peek,64,short-heavy,0.83,8,22,40,12000
A100,us-east,evict-first,64,short-heavy,0.79,10,28,55,13000
H100,eu-west,peek,64,short-heavy,0.85,7,18,35,13500
H100,eu-west,evict-first,64,short-heavy,0.81,9,24,50,14000
A100,us-east,peek,256,long-tail,0.61,20,75,210,4800
A100,us-east,evict-first,256,long-tail,0.66,22,68,180,5200
H100,eu-west,peek,256,long-tail,0.63,18,70,195,5200
H100,eu-west,evict-first,256,long-tail,0.68,20,65,170,5600
```

vikram: notes: peek keeps higher KV hit rate for mixed seqlen because it prefetches conservatively, but when memory pressure causes paging we see p99 spikes. evict-first sacrifices hit rate but lets batching keep tokens/s up at high conc.

ellen: can you drop the seqlen distribution you used and which kernel set you ran?

vikram: seqlen distro = short:40%, med:35%, long:25%. kernels = cuBLAS matmul + custom attention kernels (v3), kv-allocator v2.1, async IO prefetch ON.

maria: :thinking_face: interesting that evict-first has higher throughput at 256 conc despite lower hit rate — maybe better batch packing. do we have per-token cost estimates?

vikram: quick cost calc from run: peek long-tail ~= $0.016/token-equivalent, evict-first long-tail ~= $0.014/token-equivalent (estim backfilled from tokens_s + GPU cost profile). will run a proper cost vs latency curve.

ryan: can we test region failover (us->eu) effects and HBM pressure traces? curious if kernel selection changes failover p99.

infra-bot: deploy/bench job #84721 finished. artifacts: https://ci.redwood/84721 (benchboard + perf traces)

vikram: thanks — I'll upload PNGs & hbm traces to the benchboard and open follow-up for kernel sweep. Next action: try adaptive prefetch window that grows on low pressure and shrinks when paging detected.
